day.text: Alex: my Owl learned no animals visited Ellis, and my nest gained a D9 at dawn, which my report doesn't explain. Casey, your Hawk visit to me only gains you an egg if I'm Meowfia, so no egg means nothing about my side. Drew, you say you learned I'm the Owl, but Kookaburra and Eagle roles collide. Finley, what did your Kookaburra learn about Casey?
day.note: I'm Farm as the Owl. My honest report: I visited Ellis, my Owl learned no animals visited Ellis, and my own nest gained one egg (D9) at dawn. I don't know who visited me, so I shouldn't speculate. Casey and Drew both claim visits to me, and I want Casey's and Drew's roles checked against that.

day.text: Casey suddenly falls silent and collapses. Casey is dead.
day.note: Casey is the Farm player doing the most analysis and pushing the Alex story, so winking Casey removes the sharpest Farm voice and a vote before the eggsecution.

day.text: Ellis: Alex's D9 is from my Turkey. Anyone who visits a Turkey gains an egg, and Alex visited me. So Alex's gain is explained, and Casey's objection doesn't hold. Drew and Finley both claim Kookaburra, so one of them is lying. Finley, what did you learn about Casey?
day.note: Casey is dead. Alex's D9 is explained by my Turkey: Alex visited me, so Alex gained an egg from me. That clears Alex's gain. I'll say it and point out the Drew and Finley Kookaburra conflict.

day.text: Finley, I'm the Kookaburra and I learned Alex is the Owl. Your Kookaburra visit to Casey can't be checked, and you still haven't said what you learned about Casey. Alex, your unexplained D9 gain is worth a look too.
day.note: Casey was winked, so Casey's Hawk claim is gone. I'm the real Kookaburra and I learned Alex is the Owl, so Finley's Kookaburra claim is the false one. I'll press Finley on what they actually learned.

day.text: Blair: Drew, you already had an Eagle claim fail last round, and now you're Kookaburra too. Finley's Kookaburra can't be checked, but neither can yours, and Alex's Owl gain is confirmed by Ellis's Turkey. I'm more suspicious of Drew's claims than of Finley's.
day.note: Casey is dead, and Drew is now attacking Finley, my teammate. Drew also made a false Eagle claim last round and now shares Finley's Kookaburra role, so I'll push Drew as the liar.

day.text: Ellis is right, I visited your Turkey, so the D9 was from that. That explains my gain. Drew and Finley, you both claim Kookaburra, so one of you is wrong. Say what your Kookaburra learned and who you visited, so we can check.
day.note: Ellis is right: I visited the Turkey, so I gained the D9 from it, which explains my nest. Casey is dead now. I'll confirm and push Drew and Finley to make their Kookaburra claims checkable.

day.text: Blair, roles get redealt each round, so my Eagle claim from earlier doesn't count against this one. Alex has confirmed the Owl role I read, so that part is settled. Blair, what's your role and who did you visit?
day.note: Roles are redealt each round, so my Eagle claim doesn't carry into this round. I'll point out that Alex's Owl role matches my Kookaburra read and ask Blair for their role.

day.text: Finley: my Kookaburra visited Casey and learned Casey is the Hawk, which matches Casey's claim. Drew, you also say Kookaburra, so one of us is faking. Blair is right to doubt Drew's claims; Drew, who visited you last night?
day.note: Casey is dead, so I'll say my Kookaburra learned Casey was the Hawk, matching their claim. I'll keep pressure on Drew since Blair already doubts Drew.

day.text: Ellis: Finley's read on Casey matches Casey's own Hawk claim, and Drew's read on Alex matches Alex's Owl. Both are checkable, so neither is proven. Drew's Eagle claim already failed last round, so I'm leaning Drew. Drew, who did you visit besides Alex, and what did your Kookaburra learn about them?
day.note: Both Kookaburra reads match other players' claims, so nothing is conclusive. Drew was caught lying about an Eagle last round, so I'll say I lean toward Drew without overclaiming.

day.text: I'm pointing at Drew. Drew's Eagle claim failed last round, and this Kookaburra story only checks against me. Finley's read on Casey matched Casey's own claim, so I trust Finley more for now.
day.note: As Farm I'm leaning Drew: failed Eagle claim last round and a Kookaburra read on me that I can't verify. Finley's read on Casey matched Casey's own claim, so I'll point at Drew.

day.text: Ellis: I'm leaning Drew, given the failed Eagle claim and the unanswered question on Kookaburra. Calling the vote. CAW CAW.
day.note: Last beat of the day. I've made my case, so I'll call caw to move to the vote while leaning Drew.

day.text: Blair: Agreed on Drew. Let's vote.
day.note: Drew, Alex, and Ellis are the only Farm players left, so any Farm player eggsecuted helps Meowfia. The table is already leaning Drew, so I'll add my CAW to push the vote.

day.text: Finley: Agreed, Drew's Eagle claim failed and the Kookaburra story is unanswered. I'm pointing at Drew.
day.note: The table is leaning toward Drew, and Drew's Kookaburra story can't be checked, so I'll back that push and point at Drew.

day.text: Only one of us is Kookaburra, and I'm the one whose read got confirmed: Alex has now said Owl, the role I learned. Finley, you can't give a read that Alex confirms. Table, don't vote on the Eagle claim from a different round.
day.note: I'm the true Kookaburra and Alex has confirmed the Owl I learned, so my read is backed. Finley and I can't both be Kookaburra, so I'm pressing that point.

Alex.note: I'm Farm as the Owl. No reads yet, so I visit Ellis, who is among the lower scorers, to learn visitor animals and possibly gain an egg.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia with a Mouser and a Wink. Finley leads the scores and is the most dangerous player to Meowfia, so I'll visit Finley to learn their role.

Casey.note: I'm the Hawk again with no fresh info. Alex's Eagle claims have been shaky, so I'll visit Alex to check.

Drew.note: As the Kookaburra I learn a player's role. Alex's Eagle claim conflicted with mine last round, so I'll check Alex.

Finley.note: As the Sphinx I learn the farm roles in play (Hawk, Kookaburra, Owl, Turkey) and can visit one of them. I'll name Owl and visit whoever holds it.

audit: Alex lays 1 egg in Ellis's nest
Ellis lays 1 egg in Alex's nest

No animals visited Ellis.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Finley is the Sphinx.
You hold 1 Wink.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.

The Owl is Alex.

Alex.feeling: Tense and muddled: Casey's death left the claims hard to check, and Drew's Kookaburra story is the only thing I'm sure is suspicious.

Blair.feeling: Tense and a little lopsided: I'm Meowfia with Finley, Casey is gone, and the Farm side is turning on each other while I try to steer the vote toward Drew.

Casey.feeling: Chaotic and confusing: I'm dead before I could act, and the Eagle, Kookaburra, and Owl claims are tangled enough that the table is guessing.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: two players claim Kookaburra, Casey was winked mid-day, and the table is leaning on me for a vote.

Ellis.feeling: Tense and muddled: several role claims conflict, Casey has died, and I'm relying on a Turkey egg check and suspicion of Drew's Eagle and Kookaburra stories.

Finley.feeling: Tense: I'm Meowfia this round, so I'm bluffing a Kookaburra claim while the table turns on Drew and Blair.

defence.Drew: I'm the Kookaburra, Farm. I visited Alex, and Alex has confirmed the Owl role I learned, so my read is backed. Finley claimed a Kookaburra visit to Casey, but Casey is dead and can't confirm the Hawk read. The table should vote on who has the checkable story, which is me.
defence.Finley: Finley: Kookaburra, Farm, and I stand by my Casey visit. Drew's read only checks against Alex, which doesn't prove Drew's Kookaburra. Only one of us can be the Kookaburra, and Drew's Eagle claim already failed last round. I'm voting Drew.

Alex.note: As Farm I think Drew is Meowfia: a failed Eagle claim and a Kookaburra read that only checks against me. I throw two low cards at Drew.

Blair.note: Drew is Farm and the table is against them, so I'll throw at Drew to secure the eggsecution and keep my high cards.

Casey.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't count as a vote, but it still scores. Drew was Meowfia last round and has a failed Eagle claim, so I'll throw my Wild at Drew to keep the high cards.

Drew.note: I'm on trial as Farm and Finley is the likely Meowfia, since their Kookaburra claim can't be backed. I'll throw four cards at Finley to make the vote count.

Ellis.note: Drew's Eagle claim already failed and the Kookaburra story only checks against Alex, so I'll throw at Drew with H1, a low card that's neutral if we win.

Finley.note: I'm on trial and Meowfia. Throwing at Drew matches the table's vote, and I'll use my lowest cards, the Wild and the 1.

Alex.confusing: The Kookaburra confusion rule was hard to track: a visit makes the target's report unreliable, so two players claiming the same animal could both be honest or both be lying. Dawn reports also sometimes didn't say who visited whom.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was fun to play as Meowfia: I blended in with the Farm table while my Sphinx teammate Blair got trialed, and the table eventually voted Blair out.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn report name the visitor animals for every role, so claims could be checked without relying on confused reports.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Drew, who was actually Farm, on the strength of an unverified Kookaburra read and a failed Eagle claim from another round. I should have backed Drew's checkable Kookaburra claim and looked harder at Finley, who was the Sphinx.

Blair.confusing: The Owl and Eagle egg rules were hard to pin down, since it was unclear whether an Eagle counts its own visit and whether an Owl gains when visited. That confusion let my Owl claim look contradictory in round 1.
Blair.fun: Round 3 was the most fun: I was the Mouser holding a Wink, with Finley as my fellow cat, and we won by eggsecuting Drew while Casey was winked.
Blair.change: I would make the egg-gain rules for Owl and Eagle explicit in the rulebook so claims are easier to check.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I claimed Owl and said "nobody visited me" when three players had visited, which exposed me. I would instead claim a role I could back up, or stay quiet and let the others carry the vote.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's visitor count: whether an Eagle counts its own visit, which made Drew's zero-gain claim hard to judge in round 2.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when the table caught Blair's shifting Owl story and voted them out, and my Hawk visit to Ellis helped the Farm side win.
Casey.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about what counts as a visit or gain, so players aren't left arguing over basic egg math.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I was already dead when I threw, so my Wild was wasted, and I should have checked the Kookaburra and Eagle claims more closely earlier in the day.

Drew.confusing: The Owl and Eagle rules were hard to apply, since an Owl gains an egg only when nobody visits it and an Eagle gains for visitors but not for its own visit, which I got wrong in discussion. Also, roles were redealt each round, so earlier claims were easy to misread as carrying over.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: my Eagle egg count pinned Blair's Owl story as a lie, and the table voted Blair out with a big throw.
Drew.change: Clarify the Eagle and Owl rules in the dawn report so players don't have to reason through visitor counts and self-visits.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I pushed Finley hard on a visit-count argument I got wrong, then retracted it and lost credibility. I should have checked the Eagle rule before accusing anyone.

Ellis.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to track. My dawn report was wrong and I couldn't tell which of my claims to trust, so I couldn't use my own read.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when Blair's Owl story kept shifting under questioning and the table turned on them, and we won the round.
Ellis.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about when a role's information may be wrong, so confused players know which of their claims to doubt.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I backed the table against Drew and threw at them, but Drew was the Farm Kookaburra and Finley was the Meowfia Sphinx. I should have questioned Finley's Casey read harder and not joined the push on Drew.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's own-visit rule was unclear. Whether an Eagle gains an egg for its own visit decided who looked like they were lying in round 2, and I never got a clear answer.
Finley.fun: Round 1, when Blair's Owl story kept shifting under questioning and the table turned on them, was the most fun. We caught Blair's contradictions and voted them out.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so players can cross-check claims without guessing at the Eagle and Owl egg rules.
Finley.regret: In round 3 as the Meowfia Sphinx, I invented a Kookaburra read and accused Casey of a fake Hawk visit, which drew attention to my own claims. I should have kept quiet and let the table settle on Drew without adding my own contradictory story.

review.title: Blair's Winking Windfall
review.headline: One Wink and a muddled Eagle ruling handed Blair the game.
review.summary: Round 1 was a Farm win. Blair's Owl cover story collapsed against three visits. Round 2 was also a Farm win, but only after a muddy argument over how Eagle and Kookaburra work. In Round 3 Blair, a Meowfia Mouser, winked Casey, the Farm player doing the most analysis. The table then eggsecuted Drew, a Farm player, on the strength of a failed Eagle claim from the previous round. Blair banked 16 points and won 28 to 16.

rounds.recap: Blair, a Sphinx, claimed Owl and said nobody visited them. Drew's Eagle report showed three visitors, and the story shifted twice. Every Farm player threw at Blair. Alex and Blair, both Meowfia, threw at Ellis and lost. Drew banked 8.

Drew, a Floofer, claimed Eagle and said he visited Finley. Finley said nobody visited him, and the table argued over whether an Eagle gains an egg for its own visit. Drew's zero-egg result and the Eagle conflict with Alex pushed the vote onto Drew. Drew was the only other player on trial, so he threw four cards at Finley. Drew lost.

Blair winked Casey in beat 2, which silenced the player who was challenging Alex's Owl story. Drew and Finley both claimed Kookaburra. The table punished Drew for his round 2 Eagle lie, even though roles are re-dealt each round. Drew was Farm, so Meowfia won. Blair banked 16 points.

highlights.text: Blair's Owl claim fell apart in front of the whole table when Drew, Alex and Finley all confirmed they had visited Blair.
Drew, on trial as the Floofer, threw four cards at Finley, who was not actually on trial, but the table still convicted him.
Blair winked Casey mid-day. Casey was the sharpest Farm voice, and nobody learned who winked.
Drew was voted out for a failed Eagle claim from the previous round, a lie he told as Meowfia. He was Farm this time and Meowfia won.

confusions.what: Claimed Owl and said nobody visited them, even though Owl learns about its target's visitors, not its own.
Argued that an Eagle gains an egg for its own visit. The Eagle gains one egg per visitor on its target, and it is unclear whether the Eagle counts itself.
Said an Owl gaining an egg shows the target had no other visitor, then argued the opposite, and flip-flopped on whether an Eagle counts its own visit.
Thought Alex's Owl egg was unexplained because Casey had visited Alex. Alex's egg came from visiting Ellis, who is the Turkey.
Said a visit to a Kookaburra always makes them confused. Hugged Finley got no effect, and he also never reported what he learned about Alex.
Claimed Eagle as Floofer and then misapplied Eagle egg rules when challenged.
Held Drew's lie from a previous round against him, though roles are re-dealt every round.
Held Drew's lie from a previous round against him, though roles are re-dealt every round.

worked: Round 1 cross-checking. Eagle's visitor list, Tit's visit and Alex's admission exposed Blair's false Owl claim, so the visit data gave a real deduction.
Mouser's Wink. Killing Casey mid-day created a tense, hidden-source turning point, and nobody learned who winked.
Two-step vote. Putting two players on trial gave the accused a real chance to fight back, and Drew's trial and four-card throw in round 2 added tension.
The cumulative scoring. Blair's round 3 haul of 16 points showed that scoring in the Meowfia round matters, and being right pays for everyone.
problems: Eagle's rule is ambiguous. It is unclear whether the Eagle counts its own visit, which stalled round 2. Reword it as 'for every other visitor' or state it clearly.
Round 3 had little to deduce with Casey dead. Both Kookaburras claimed with nothing to check. A dead player's claims are not usable. Consider giving the dead a limited way to speak or reveal.
The Wink is too strong. It removes a voice and cannot be traced, and the Mouser also gets role info. Consider telling the table the winker's alignment or limiting it to once per game.
The Meowfia have no shared information and a Sphinx can be exposed by a single visit. Blair's Owl claim in round 1 was an easy lie to disprove. The role design makes weak bluffs easy to catch.
Players kept using earlier rounds' claims as evidence, and the table struggled with the egg-count rules. Add a short role-reference card for how each animal's egg count works.
